citation: Fencil person-color-values and the pinned Ghostty ANSI Name enum in deps/ghostty/src/terminal/color.zig.
why: The core stores a palette name and the shell looks up its ANSI slot. The same cases hold the core to the supported names and the shell to their slot order and stored spelling.

cases.name: red uses slot 1
cases.why: Slot 0 is ANSI black. The first supported name starts at slot 1.

cases.name: green uses slot 2
cases.why: Store the name so green follows changes to ANSI slot 2.

cases.name: yellow uses slot 3
cases.why: Store the name so yellow follows changes to ANSI slot 3.

cases.name: blue uses slot 4
cases.why: Store the name so blue follows changes to ANSI slot 4.

cases.name: magenta uses slot 5
cases.why: Store the name so magenta follows changes to ANSI slot 5.

cases.name: cyan uses slot 6
cases.why: Cyan is the last ANSI hue offered by name.

cases.name: lowercase hex stores and draws the exact RGB
cases.why: An exact RGB stays fixed even when the terminal palette changes.

cases.name: mixed-case hex is normalized before storage
cases.why: The core accepts mixed case in a request. The shell draws the canonical lowercase value it receives in the roster.

cases.name: an empty value clears the assigned color
cases.why: The shell sends a clear as an empty string and the roster uses it for an uncolored subject.

cases.name: none clears the assigned color
cases.why: The CLI spells a clear as none. The word itself draws no color.

cases.name: ANSI white has no assigned name
cases.why: Exact RGB can represent white. Assigning by name offers the six ANSI hues.

cases.name: named colors are lowercase
cases.why: Palette names have one spelling in the core and the shell.

cases.name: hex requires six digits
cases.why: Three-digit shorthand cannot be stored as the exact RGB format.

cases.name: hex rejects nonhex digits
cases.why: Matching the length and prefix alone would let an unrenderable color through.

cases.name: hex requires the hash prefix
cases.why: The prefix identifies the stored string as RGB.
